sections.html:
Find the Register and Recorder at the courthouse, 1168 Liberty Street, Franklin, PA 16323, or write to P.O. Box 831. Weekday hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with legal holidays off.

One elected official fills three roles here: Register of Wills, Clerk of Orphans' Court and Recorder. Probate papers, marriage licenses and land records therefore share a single counter. Anyone selling a house they inherited may need it for both reasons in one trip.

Venango County recorder at a glance
QuestionAnswer
Street address1168 Liberty Street, Franklin, PA 16323
Mailing addressP.O. Box 831
HoursWeekdays, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed legal holidays
Electronic recordingCSC eRecording Solutions, 866-652-0111
State transfer tax1 percent of value

The county accepts electronic filings, which CSC eRecording Solutions processes. Their number is 866-652-0111. Closing agents and attorneys favor this route because it avoids the drive to Franklin and the days a letter spends in the mail. It also helps when buyer and seller sign in different towns.

Recording fees vary by document. Ask the office for its fee list, or look at the Recorder of Deeds fee schedule in the county's document library. Phone for the precise amount on your own deed before any payment goes out.

Payment is due when the deed goes on file with the recorder. Pennsylvania takes 1 percent of the value, and the person giving the deed and the person getting it are each answerable for it. Your municipality or school district can tack on more.

  • Exemptions cover some gifts within a family, deeds to government bodies and houses that pass under a will or by intestacy.
  • Who pays in practice comes from the sales contract, so study that clause before you sign.

Franklin and Oil City are the only cities. Everything else is a borough or township. The local share follows the parcel, so learn which municipality and school district yours falls in before you guess at your proceeds.

The county has shrunk steadily since 1950, when 65,328 people lived here. The count was 50,454 in 2020 and is estimated at 49,346 now, a fall of 2.2 percent. There are 26,293 housing units for 21,397 households, and 75.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

Owned homes are valued at $119,800 for a typical one. Rent at the midpoint is $795 a month, household income at the midpoint is $61,522, and 27.2 percent of residents are 65 or older. Prices this low cap what a fixer-upper can bring, and repair bills can swallow the profit. Little is being built, so existing houses carry the market.

sections.h2: Old deeds, easements and mineral questions
sections.html:
The oil industry started in this region, and many parcels carry the paperwork to prove it: aged deeds, old easements and mineral questions. If your family has held the land for generations, ask the title company to check for recorded easements, rights of way and releases early.

An older house in Franklin or Oil City will draw an inspector's attention to its foundation, wiring and plumbing, so expect those questions.

sections.h2: Which municipality is your house in?
sections.html:
Franklin is the county seat and Oil City is the largest place. Boroughs include Sugar Creek, Pleasantville, Polk, Emlenton, Rouseville, Clintonville, Cooperstown, Barkeyville and Utica. Cranberry and Cornplanter are the most populous townships.

Each of these governs itself, which means zoning, permits and tax shares differ by address. Phone the office for your street before you list and ask what buyers or inspectors tend to raise. The recorder's staff can also confirm your municipality and school district.

Real estate tax rates are posted on the county's Real Estate Tax Millages page, with one PDF for every year from 2005 through 2026. Open the newest and look up your municipality and school district. For the assessed value behind your bill, visit the Tax Assessment Office in the courthouse complex.

Buyers want these figures, so hand your latest bill to the title company early. When repairs on an old house would cost more than the market returns, selling as-is for cash avoids them.

Estate houses start with the Register of Wills, who runs probate and collects the Commonwealth's inheritance tax. Here that person also records deeds. Decide who may sign before a closing is booked, and ask the recorder which forms apply, since a transfer by will or intestacy can escape transfer tax.

One counter does both jobs, so an executor can often start probate and raise recording questions in a single visit. Carry the estate papers, the old deed and the newest tax bill.

Finish the paperwork before the first showing. Locate the deed and confirm its names match the people who will sign. Add your last tax bill, a payoff figure from your lender and a quick title company search for old liens, releases and easements. Each takes one call, and each removes a surprise that could stall a closing.

Then tour the house the way a buyer would, and collect receipts for any work you have done.

Listing can fetch more, yet with values this modest the difference from an as-is sale can shrink after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs. Cash works well for inherited or vacant houses and for owners on a clock. Collect written offers, with dates and proof of funds, and compare what each would net.

sections.h2: From accepted offer to recorded deed
sections.html:
Accepting an offer sets work in motion. Your title company or attorney asks for payoff figures, checks title for easements and releases and writes the deed. A notary witnesses your signature at closing. The deed is then filed, either online through CSC eRecording Solutions or at the Liberty Street counter, with the tax paid at filing. The Recorder indexes it and the buyer becomes the owner of record.

A cash buyer sidesteps the lender's appraisal and loan approval, so the schedule is shorter, though title work and recording remain. Afterward, store the tax bill, payoff letter and recorded deed together.

If you mail the deed instead of filing electronically, allow extra days for it to reach the office. Electronic filing avoids that wait, which is one reason title companies prefer it. Either way, do not let a signed package sit on a desk after closing, and ask your title agent to confirm the filing went through.

If a question comes up on closing day, have the title agent phone the recorder first. One call costs less than a rejected filing.

faqs.q: When is the Venango County recorder open?
faqs.a: The courthouse office at 1168 Liberty Street in Franklin keeps weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Legal holidays are closed.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available in Venango County?
faqs.a: Yes. Electronic real estate filings go through CSC eRecording Solutions, 866-652-0111, and your title company or attorney can usually set it up.

faqs.q: Where are the Venango County recording fees listed?
faqs.a: The county posts a Recorder of Deeds fee schedule in its document library, and the Register and Recorder's office can give you its fees by phone. Call before you send a check.

faqs.q: Who handles probate for a Venango County house?
faqs.a: The Register of Wills, who also collects inheritance tax for the Commonwealth. In Venango County that role is combined with the Recorder and the Clerk of Orphans' Court.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rate applies in Venango County?
faqs.a: The state's rate is 1 percent of value. Local shares may be added by your municipality and school district, so get the combined figure for your parcel from the recorder.
